content:
incident-bot: [pager] SEV-2: streaming/function-call error rate spike in production (svc: inference-api, route: /v1/generate stream). Alerts from 3 regions. Example symptom: clients see SSE disconnects and subsequent tool-call JSON parse errors. Auto-pager triggered.
Morgan (on-call): I'm on it, pulling up dashboards. Which orgs are hit?
Priya Patel: seeing elevated 502s during streaming sessions for orgs: acme, grover-ai, and two internal test tenants. Error trace: 'Unexpected end of JSON input' coming from tool-call parser after SSE disconnect.
Jake Morales: looks like disconnects happen right after long tool-call payloads (>8kB). Might be chunk boundary issue.
Sam Kline: confirming. Repro on staging with client v2.3.1 where stream truncates at ~8192 bytes.
Alice Chen: memory? nginx proxy? TCP resets? Don't assume. Collect logs and timeline first.
Morgan (on-call): ok prioritized checklist: 1) collect stream logs from proxy and runtime 2) identify earliest failing commit/deploy 3) mitigation (non-stream fallback + routing) 4) customer comms. Assigning tasks: Priya->logs, Jake->runtime trace, Sam->repro and client-check, Alice->proxy config + infra. Eli watch for deploys.
Priya Patel: logs pulled: https://logs.redwood.dev/s/1791234567/stream-err.gz (access limited). Pasted sample here:
```
[2026-10-03T14:42:11.122Z] INFO SSE->client chunk-size=4096 seq=127
[2026-10-03T14:42:11.124Z] INFO SSE->client chunk-size=4096 seq=128
[2026-10-03T14:42:11.125Z] WARN connection reset by peer id=xyz123
[2026-10-03T14:42:11.126Z] ERROR tool-call-parser: Unexpected end of JSON input
[2026-10-03T14:42:11.126Z] INFO dropping partial buffer session=abc-789
```
Priya Patel: note chunk sizes are 4k, so a long payload spans multiple chunks. There is a reset between seq 128 and the parser error.
Sam Kline: reproduced on staging with curl + --no-buffer; when we simulate an abrupt client close between chunks, parser throws the same error. Means parser isn't tolerant to incomplete final chunk.
Jake Morales: runtime got an internal change last week: a commit to the streaming buffer plumbing (commit f0a3b4) introduced a fast-path that avoids reassembly for performance. Suspect it fails to reassemble when early disconnects happen.
Eli Torres: deploy-bot shows a rolling deploy at 2026-10-03T03:20:00 UTC that included f0a3b4.
deploy-bot: rollout f0a3b4 -> production (25%) at 2026-10-03T03:20:00Z, 100% at 03:28:00Z.
Alice Chen: infra sidenote: we updated an nginx config two days ago (keepalive timeout lowered to 30s) but this looks timing-related not timeout. Notable: affected connections spike under heavy concurrent streaming.
Morgan (on-call): initial hypothesis list (in-thread):
- H1: streaming fast-path regression (f0a3b4) fails to reassemble multi-chunk tool-call messages on client disconnect -> parser sees truncated JSON.
- H2: reverse proxy (nginx) aggressively terminates idle chunked streaming connections during high concurrency causing partial frames.
- H3: some client versions send malformed chunk boundaries that used to be tolerated but now hit the fast-path bug.
We'll collect evidence per hypothesis.
Priya Patel: evidence for H1: trace shows buffer drop code path executed right after connection reset. Code pointer: runtime/streaming/fastpath.go:line 214.
Jake Morales: reproducer patch ready. I'll run a build with fast-path disabled to validate.
Sam Kline: repro steps (staging):
1) start streaming API with large tool-call payload (10kB)
2) client closes socket mid-stream
3) observe parser error in runtime logs
Commands:
```bash
# spin up local server
make run-local && curl -N 'https://local:8080/v1/generate?stream=true' -d @large_payload.json
# simulate abrupt close
sleep 0.1; pkill -f curl
```
Jake Morales: ran build with fast-path off, staging run shows no parser error when client disconnects mid-stream. That strongly supports H1.
Morgan (on-call): mitigation choices:
- quick rollback of f0a3b4 to previous build (fast but needs canary and deploy windows)
- runtime patch: make parser tolerant to truncated chunks (requires code change + test, faster than full rollback maybe)
- infra mitigation: enable non-stream fallback per org (switch to buffered non-SSE responses) for impacted orgs until fix.
Priya Patel: customer impact estimate: roughly 2.8% of active streaming sessions experienced disconnect+parse error in the last 4 hours. Affected customers: acme (3 endpoints), grover-ai (1 high-volume endpoint). CS-ops ready to reach out.
CS-ops: preparing post to customers with affected sessions, ETA for workaround ~1.5 hr if we flip non-stream fallback.
Jake Morales: I'll open a build with a defensive parser change (ensure reassembly of partial chunks even after connection resets) and test. If green, we can ship a quick patch to production as a patch release (no major infra changes).
Alice Chen: network team suggests we can flip an nginx flag to increase proxy buffering for streaming endpoints, but it's risky across all tenants. Prefer per-org non-stream fallback.
Morgan (on-call): action plan now:
- Jake: hotfix parser patch (priority) -> aim to prod in 2 hrs if tests pass
- Priya: enable non-stream fallback for acme and grover-ai via routing rule (feature flag) now to stop further errors
- Sam: continue client compatibility check; list client versions that could be impacted
- Alice: monitor proxies and provide metrics for aborted connections
- Eli: hold deploy window and coordinate patch rollout
- CS-ops: send proactive notice to impacted customers
Jake Morales: hotfix PR opened: https://git.redwood.dev/r/streaming/+/PR-3421. Patch changes: reassembly fallback on disconnect + unit tests.
Priya Patel: toggled feature-flag: org:acme non-stream=true, org:grover-ai non-stream=true. Confirming reduction in errors for acme after 60s.
Morgan (on-call): good. Now timeline update for RCA tracking:
- 2026-10-03T03:20:00Z -> deploy f0a3b4 roll to prod (deploy-bot)
- 2026-10-03T14:40:00Z -> monitoring alerts triggered (error rate up)
- 2026-10-03T14:42:00Z -> incident pager fired (incident-bot)
- 2026-10-03T14:45:00Z -> on-call assigned (Morgan)
- 2026-10-03T15:05:00Z -> reproducer validated on staging (Sam/Jake)
- 2026-10-03T15:20:00Z -> non-stream fallback enabled for 2 orgs (Priya)
- 2026-10-03T16:10:00Z -> hotfix PR opened (Jake)
- 2026-10-03T17:30:00Z -> prod hotfix roll scheduled (pending tests)
Jake Morales: test results: unit + integration green locally, staging pass with reproducer. Requesting canary rollout 10% then 100% after 15m.
Eli Torres: scheduled patch rollout at 2026-10-03T17:45:00Z for 10% canary. Will monitor error rates.
deploy-bot: rollout PR-3421 -> canary 10% at 2026-10-03T17:45:00Z.
Morgan (on-call): handoff note for next on-call: if canary shows stabilization (errors down to baseline) then proceed to 100% and close the incident. If errors persist or other orgs affected, prepare rollback.
Sam Kline: client compatibility: list of client versions that may be tolerant: v2.3.0 and earlier had reassembly behavior; v2.3.1 changed buffering behavior and surfaced bug. Reach out to client-eng for a coordinated upgrade plan.
Priya Patel: post-mitigation check: after flag and canary, observed error rate drop from 2.8% -> 0.2% for flagged orgs. Non-flagged orgs still show 0.9% until hotfix completes.
CS-ops: customer comms sent: "We identified intermittent streaming disconnects causing tool-call failures for a subset of streaming sessions. We have applied a temporary mitigation and are deploying a permanent fix. We'll follow up with a full RCA."
Morgan (on-call): closing checklist for now: 1) continue monitoring for 2 more hours 2) write timeline and add to postmortem 3) assign owner for root-cause write-up (Jake + Priya) 4) code review and followup tests for all streaming clients.
Jake Morales: assigning myself + Priya for RCA write-up. Initial root cause: regression in streaming reassembly fast-path introduced in f0a3b4 that didn't handle mid-stream disconnects -> produced truncated JSON to tool-call parser. Secondary factor: newer client versions change buffering semantics and exposed the regression.
Morgan (on-call): leaving a short on-call handoff note -> next on-call Eli (from 18:00Z). If errors climb above 1% sustained, escalate immediately.
Eli Torres: acked. I'll watch deploy healthboard and alert if canary diverges.
incident-bot: incident noted as active. SUMMARY: active mitigation in place (org-level non-stream fallback), hotfix PR-3421 in rollout. Next update due in 30m or on status change.
